summary: The latest announcement feed contains three substantial heavy-ion contributions: a virtuality-resolved factorization framework for in-medium jet functions, a validated 3D stochastic solver for relativistic relaxation-time kinetics, and an order-hbar-squared thermodynamic analysis that favors the kinetic pseudo-gauge for spin hydrodynamics. Physics-AI value is led by real detector-data releases and calibrated sampling or dynamics methods, with transfer limits stated explicitly.
professional_summary: Virtuality-resolved jet functions; stochastic relativistic transport and kinetic attractors; pseudo-gauge consistency in spin hydrodynamics; public detector waveforms; FAIR and AI-ready data; likelihood-corrected Boltzmann sampling; stochastic trajectory generation.
strongest_paper_summary: The jet-function paper supplies the day's most consequential heavy-ion result, with an explicit derivation, recovery of standard BDMPS-Z limits, numerical exploration, and a clear accounting of approximations.

papers.title: Factorization and virtuality evolution of jet functions in heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: Derives a factorized gamma+jet cross section with an in-medium jet function differential in initial virtuality. Integration reproduces standard BDMPS-Z results, while finite virtuality exposes the transition between vacuum-like and medium-induced radiation.
papers.abstract: The framework identifies the medium-formation-time to jet-formation-time ratio as the control variable for relevant initial virtualities, under a Glauber, soft-radiation, eikonal setup.

papers.title: ShARK: A Stochastic Transport Framework for the Relativistic Relaxation Time Approximation Boltzmann Equation
papers.summary: Constructs a 3D continuous-momentum Monte Carlo solver from microcanonical stochastic collisions and validates it against exact Bjorken and Gubser kinetic solutions plus convergence tests on an optical-Glauber O-O profile.
papers.abstract: The stochastic N-body construction converges to Anderson-Witting kinetics while conserving local four-momentum event by event.

papers.title: Global equilibrium at order O(hbar^2): pseudo-gauge ambiguity, Maxwell relations, and thermodynamic consistency
papers.summary: Derives order-hbar-squared equilibrium corrections for rotating spin-half matter and finds that Maxwell relations hold in the kinetic pseudo-gauge but generally fail in canonical and GLW choices.
papers.abstract: Global charges are pseudo-gauge independent, while local densities and thermodynamic consistency are not.

papers.title: EXO-200 Public Data Release for AI/ML Applications
papers.summary: Releases roughly one million real calibration events with raw charge and light waveforms paired to reconstructed event quantities in HDF5.
papers.abstract: The resource enables reproducible detector-ML work, although benchmark tasks and detector-condition coverage remain to be developed.

papers.title: Toward FAIR and AI-Ready Data: An Assessment of the GlueX Experiment's Data Ecosystem at Jefferson Lab
papers.summary: Defines deterministic FAIR and AI-readiness criteria and applies them to the GlueX data ecosystem, separating general-purpose checks from experiment-specific validation.
papers.abstract: A concrete governance case study with actionable recommendations, but no downstream evidence yet that the metrics predict ML utility.

papers.title: Bridging Stochastic Flow Maps and Boltzmann Generators with Normalizing Flows
papers.summary: Uses exact-likelihood conditional flows to importance-correct every stochastic denoising transition, proves consistency and error propagation bounds, and improves molecular equilibrium sampling.
papers.abstract: The method is a credible candidate for lattice or Boltzmann-weighted physics sampling, but current tests do not address gauge theories, topology, or volume scaling.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Trajectory Generation from Discrete Observations with Stochasticity
papers.summary: Learns continuous probability-velocity fields from discrete stochastic snapshots without known SDE coefficients or score estimation, with convergence theory and fluid-dynamics tests.
papers.abstract: Transfer to heavy-ion evolution is plausible but depends on conservation-aware representations and scaling to high-dimensional event ensembles.

cautions.title: Landscape of pentaquark bound states with neural-network Variational Monte Carlo
cautions.summary: A systematic neural-VMC scan finds 21 candidates bound by 2-15 MeV, but the paper's own localized scattering states retain a few MeV of residual kinetic energy and no full uncertainty budget is supplied.
cautions.abstract: The computational scan is useful, but the weakest shallow-binding claims are comparable to unresolved numerical and model scales.
